original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it.

first_step.inspect: Read Model section 1 of the three-register bound and identify the exact excluded free operations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: For any number of auxiliary scalar registers, prove and attain the exact mW rank-one call minimum for W data targets C_i in the full lattice q^-1 M_m(Z), with fixed odd q and each q C_i mod 2 invertible, when all paid address frames lie in that lattice. Specialize the construction and replay to m=W=3.
scope_change_reason: The selector card asks whether a larger register model escapes the three-register obstruction. I narrow the address alphabet to one full odd-denominator lattice, where a square-zero augmentation tests arbitrary relation rank and auxiliary count. The excluded even-denominator frames are a precise remaining escape route.
bottleneck_link: Shows whether any extra-register call saving is possible without dyadic address frames. It rules out an entire formal mechanism class while leaving the denominator feature needed for a new bit primitive explicit.
stop_rule: Finish the uniform square-zero rank proof, exact nine-call witness for the pinned three-role target, and boundary/tamper controls; stop without searching dyadic frames.
evidence: PROOF.md gives the uniform rank bound and tight column construction; RESULT.json and verify.py replay the exact nine-call instance, source pins, and boundary/tamper controls. The verifier ran on Python 3.14.7; the repository's registered Python 3.12 replay could not run locally because 3.12 is unavailable.
author: Cinna Davis
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in mathematical derivation, implementation, verification, and writing; no subagents or independent human review.

open_questions.question: Can even-denominator address frames use auxiliary registers to beat mW calls while preserving the same data endpoints?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The theorem isolates the denominator class any extra-register saving would have to leave, but does not test whether such a construction is useful for the bit supplier.
open_questions.first_step: Start with one dyadic denominator and two explicit frame relations; derive an exact call word and full auxiliary boundary before any larger search.
open_questions.blocked_by: No candidate dyadic word or favorable native/recursive invoice is known.
